doc:
In a preadditive category, if the product of `X` and `Y` exists, then the
binary biproduct of `X` and `Y` exists.

In a preadditive category, if the coproduct over `f : J → C` exists,
then the biproduct over `f` exists.

If `f` is a morphism `X₁ ⊞ X₂ ⟶ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂` whose `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` entry is an isomorphism,
then we can construct isomorphisms `L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂` and `R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂`
so that `L.hom ≫ g ≫ R.hom` is diagonal (with `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` component still `f`),
via Gaussian elimination.

(This is the version of `Biprod.gaussian` written in terms of components.)

signature.text:
def CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C]
  [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C] {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : C}
  (f₁₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (f₁₂ : X₁ ⟶ Y₂) (f₂₁ : X₂ ⟶ Y₁) (f₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) [CategoryTheory.IsIso f₁₁] :
  (L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂) ×'
    (R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) ×'
      (g₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) ×'
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp L.hom
            (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.Biprod.ofComponents f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂)
              R.hom) =
          CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map f₁₁ g₂₂

value.text:
fun {C} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C]
    [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C] {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂} f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂
    [CategoryTheory.IsIso f₁₁] =>
  ⟨CategoryTheory.Biprod.unipotentLower
      (-CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f₂₁ (CategoryTheory.inv f₁₁)),
    ⟨CategoryTheory.Biprod.unipotentUpper
        (-CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.inv f₁₁) f₁₂),
      ⟨f₂₂ -
          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f₂₁
            (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.inv f₁₁) f₁₂),
        ⋯⟩⟩⟩

any binary bicone `b` satisfying `total : b.fst ≫ b.inl + b.snd ≫ b.inr = 𝟙 b.X`.

any bicone `b` for `f` satisfying `total : ∑ j : J, b.π j ≫ b.ι j = 𝟙 b.X`.

A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) finite products
preserves finite biproducts.

If `f` is a morphism `X₁ ⊞ X₂ ⟶ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂` whose `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` entry is an isomorphism,
then we can construct isomorphisms `L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂` and `R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂`
so that `L.hom ≫ g ≫ R.hom` is diagonal (with `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` component still `f`),
via Gaussian elimination.

def CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian.{v, u} {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C]
  [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C] {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : C}
  (f : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ⟶ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂)
  [CategoryTheory.IsIso
      (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.inl
        (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.fst))] :
  (L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂) ×'
    (R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) ×'
      (g₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) ×'
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp L.hom (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f R.hom) =
          CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map
            (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.inl
              (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.fst))
            g₂₂

doc:
We will define the structure sheaf as
the subsheaf of all dependent functions in `Π x : U, Localizations R x`
consisting of those functions which can locally be expressed as a ratio of
(the images in the localization of) elements of `R`.

Quoting Hartshorne:

For an open set $U ⊆ Spec A$, we define $𝒪(U)$ to be the set of functions
$s : U → ⨆_{𝔭 ∈ U} A_𝔭$, such that $s(𝔭) ∈ A_𝔭$ for each $𝔭$,
and such that $s$ is locally a quotient of elements of $A$:
to be precise, we require that for each $𝔭 ∈ U$, there is a neighborhood $V$ of $𝔭$,
contained in $U$, and elements $a, f ∈ A$, such that for each $𝔮 ∈ V, f ∉ 𝔮$,
and $s(𝔮) = a/f$ in $A_𝔮$.

Now Hartshorne had the disadvantage of not knowing about dependent functions,
so we replace his circumlocution about functions into a disjoint union with
`Π x : U, Localizations x`.

Given a ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S`, an open set `U` of the prime spectrum of `R` and an open
set `V` of the prime spectrum of `S`, such that `V ⊆ (comap f) ⁻¹' U`, we can push a section `s`

`comap f` from the right. Explicitly, if `s` evaluates on `comap f p` to `a / b`, its image on `V`
evaluates on `p` to `f(a) / f(b)`.

we prove the predicate `isLocallyFraction` is preserved by this map, hence it can be extended to
a morphism between the structure sheaves of `R` and `S`.

For a ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S` and open sets `U` and `V` of the prime spectra of `R` and

doc:
**Noetherian case: kernels are automatically adically closed.** If `B` is a Noetherian ring,
`K`-adically complete, and the structure map `B → A` is surjective, then the kernel of `B → A`
is `K`-adically closed. The point is Krull's intersection theorem: `A` is a finite `B`-module (a
surjective image of `B`), so it is `K`-adically Hausdorff because `K` lies in the Jacobson
radical of a complete ring (`IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson`, `IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`); an
element of `B` congruent to the kernel modulo every `K ^ n` therefore maps into every
`K ^ n • ⊤` and so to `0`. This makes the closedness hypothesis of the lemmas above automatic in
the Noetherian setting (Artin–Rees, Bosch §7.3).

  (hs : Function.Surjective ⇑(algebraMap B A)) : RingHom.AdicKerClosed K (algebraMap B A)

hypothesis — and generalises `map_preimage_basicOpen` (stated for the induced `mapTop`) to an
arbitrary `f`, using the step-(a) base identification `base_toPrimeSpectrum_eq`.

**The sheaf component of an open immersion over its range is an isomorphism.**
For an open immersion `w : Spf S ⟶ Spf R` and `g : R` with `D(g) ⊆ range w.base`, the structure
sheaf `c`-component `w.c.app (op D(g))` is an isomorphism in `CommRingCat`. This is the
`PresheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.c_iso'` fact — an open immersion's component over the image of an
open is invertible — applied to the open `D(g)`, which is the image of its own preimage because it
lies in the range.

**The sheaf component of an open immersion reflects the ideal of definition over its range.**
For an open immersion `w : Spf S ⟶ Spf R` and `g t : R` with `D(g) ⊆ range w.base`, if the source
ideal of definition `J` is contained in the restriction of `I` over the range
(`hres : J ≤ Ideal.map (globalSectionsMap I J w) I` — hypothesis `(B)`) and `Ψ t ∈ J`
(`Ψ = globalSectionsMap I J w`), then `awayCompletionHom I g t ∈ awayCompletionIdeal I g`.

This is the end-to-end adic-source reflection of issue 471a: it supplies the `(A)` bijectivity input
(`bijective_arbSheafComponent`) to the merged reduction `reflects_awayCompletionIdeal_of_bijective`,
leaving only the containment `(B)` for the caller. The bare form without `(B)` is *false* — an open
immersion may shrink the ideal of definition the wrong way (the reversed cofinal iso
`Spf₍y₎ ⟶ Spf₍y²₎`); `(B)` holds for the concrete completed-localization pieces the descent
`le_comap_globalSectionsMap_of_cover` (471c / 482) covers with.

Let `J` be a finitely generated ideal of `S` and `t : S`. If the residues `ḡ` (`g ∈ T`) of a family
of elements generate the unit ideal of `S ⧸ J` (equivalently, the basic opens `D(ḡ)` cover `Spf S`)
and the section `t` vanishes on each chart `D(ḡ)`, i.e.
`awayCompletionHom J g t ∈ awayCompletionIdeal J g`, then `t ∈ J`.

**Adicity on global sections descends along an open cover of the source.**
Let `φ : Spf J ⟶ Spf I` and let `{wᵥ : Spf Lᵥ ⟶ Spf J}` be a family of open immersions whose base
images cover `Spf J`. If `J` is finitely generated, every piece's source ideal is contained in the
restriction of `J` over its range (hypothesis `(B)` `hres`), and every composite `wᵥ ≫ φ` is adic on
global sections, then `φ` itself is adic on global sections.

doc:
The data of a comonad on C consists of an endofunctor G together with natural transformations
`ε : G ⟶ 𝟭 C` and `δ : G ⟶ G ⋙ G` satisfying three equations:
- `δ_X ≫ G δ_X = δ_X ≫ δ_(GX)` (coassociativity)
- `δ_X ≫ ε_(GX) = 1_X` (left counit)
- `δ_X ≫ G ε_X = 1_X` (right counit)

doc:
The data of a monad on C consists of an endofunctor T together with natural transformations
`η : 𝟭 C ⟶ T` and `μ : T ⋙ T ⟶ T` satisfying three equations:
- `T μ_X ≫ μ_X = μ_(TX) ≫ μ_X` (associativity)
- `η_(TX) ≫ μ_X = 1_X` (left unit)
- `Tη_X ≫ μ_X = 1_X` (right unit)
